claims.text: The workflow of LLM-based multi-agent systems can be synthesized into a general structure encompassing five key components: profile, perception, self-action, mutual interaction, and evolution.
Applications of LLM-based multi-agent systems can be broadly categorized into problem-solving and world simulation.
Agent profile generation in multi-agent systems relies on contextualized generation, pre-defined methods, or learning-based methods.
Sources of perceptual information for LLM agents consist of entire environment messages, interaction messages, and self-reflection messages.
Inter-agent interaction structures can be categorized into hierarchical, decentralized, centralized, and shared message pool architectures.
Agent evolution sources comprise environment feedback, agent interaction feedback, and human feedback.

evidence.description: The paper presents a unified agent framework comprising profile, perception, self-action, mutual interaction, and evolution as five essential workflow modules.
The authors systematically review and map existing literature onto problem-solving and world simulation domains.
Section 3.1.2 categorizes agent profile creation into contextualized generation, pre-defined methods, and learning-based methods.
Section 3.2.1 categorizes perceptual message sources into entire environment message, interaction message, and self-reflection message.
Section 3.4.2 classifies communication frameworks into hierarchy, decentralized, centralized, and shared message pool structures.
Section 3.5.1 details three distinct sources of feedback guiding self-reflection: environment, agent interaction, and human feedback.

methodologies.name: Unified Five-Module LLM-MAS Taxonomy Framework
methodologies.description: A systematic survey framework organizing LLM multi-agent literature along five workflow modules: profile, perception, self-action, mutual interaction, and evolution.

limitations.text: Previous works in LLM-based multi-agent systems were independently executed and lacked a systematic and comprehensive synthesis of framework structure.
Reinforcement learning-based intelligent systems have inherent limitations in terms of adaptability and complexity.
LLMs operate as black-box systems, rendering their decision-making processes opaque and hard to evaluate in high-stakes applications.
LLMs tend to produce hallucinations, generating text that deviates from reality or contains unverified information.

future_work.text: Developing effective coordination mechanisms for collective intelligence in AI agents to avoid groupthink and cognitive biases.
Deploying LLM-based multi-agent systems as a service (AaaS) via cloud platforms while ensuring decision transparency and system stability.
Exploring efficient data fusion frameworks and algorithms for multi-agent systems operating in multi-modal, dynamic environments like healthcare and traffic management.
